● notes.md is written. Here's what's in it and why each point earns its place.

  Bullet one — structure. ANSI sequences aren't a grab-bag of magic strings; they follow a
  grammar. The dominant family is CSI: the escape byte 0x1B, a [, semicolon-separated numeric
  parameters, and a final byte that picks the operation. Once you see that shape, \x1b[31m,
  \x1b[2J, and \x1b[1;5H stop being incantations you copy from Stack Overflow and become
  something you can generate, parse, and validate. It also tells you where the sequence ends,
  which is exactly what you need to strip or rewrite it programmatically.

  Bullet two — zero display width. This is where most real bugs come from. len(s) counts the
  escape bytes, but the terminal draws none of them. Any code that pads a column, centers a
  header, wraps at 80 characters, or truncates with an ellipsis will silently misalign the
  moment color enters. The fix is to separate the styling layer from the layout layer:
  measure the plain text, then apply styling. Worth calling out explicitly because the
  failure is visual and intermittent rather than a crash, so it survives testing and shows up
  in front of users.

  Bullet three — support isn't guaranteed. The same bytes that render as red in an
